question: does ramapo have a pre-med track or do i just major in bio
answer:
Yes—there are pre-med tracks, so the choice isn’t limited to a Biology major. The catalog lists these bachelor’s majors for “bio”: Biochemistry BS; Bioinformatics BS; Biology BS [16]. The recommended plan for students admitted in 2026–2027 includes “Biology: General Pre-Med Track” [3], and Biochemistry also has a “Biochemistry/Pre-Medical Track” plan [1]. A track is an advising path of courses through a major intended to prepare students for graduate school or a professional career; it does not appear on your transcript [4].

Plans: https://www.ramapo.edu/recommended-graduation-plan-2026/tas/biology/ [3] and https://www.ramapo.edu/recommended-graduation-plan-2026/tas/biochemistry/ [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BCHM) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [16](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: does physics 1 count toward gen ed or only for my major
answer:
If by “Physics 1” you mean PHYS 111 or PHYS 116: both count toward Gen Ed 18-Scientific Reasoning (GESR), not only your major [16]. PHYS 111 FUNDAMENTALS PHYSICS I LECTURE is 4 credits; it has GESR and WRITING INTENSIVE (WRIT) attributes, and requires concurrent enrollment in PHYS 118L INTRODUCTORY PHYSICS I LAB [1]. PHYS 116 PHYSICS I WITH CALCULUS LECTURE is 4 credits; it has the GESR attribute and requires concurrent enrollment in PHYS 116L INTRODUCTORY PHYSICS I LAB [2]. PHYS 116L is 1 credit and also has the GESR attribute; it requires concurrent enrollment in PHYS 116 [3]. PHYS 116 and 116L together are 5 credits [2]. General Education courses can also count toward your major, but no more than two may double count [6].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHYS111) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHYS116) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHYS116L) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [16](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: What's the difference between the Biology major and the Biochemistry major in terms of required courses? Which one has more chem?
answer:
Biochemistry BS requires all of these chemistry courses: CHEM 117 and 117L; CHEM 211 and 211L; CHEM 213 and 213L; CHEM 324 and 324L; CHEM 350 and 350L; CHEM 425; CHEM 430; and CHEM 446. [1]

Biology BS requires CHEM 117 and 117L, plus one organic chemistry option: either CHEM 206 and 206L, or CHEM 211 and 211L plus CHEM 213 and 213L. It also requires four electives; at least one must be from the biology elective options with a lab or field component and at least one from the options without lab or field components. CHEM 425 is one option in the latter list, but it is not mandatory. [2]

So Biochemistry has more required chemistry: it requires additional chemistry courses, while Biology offers a shorter organic chemistry option and makes CHEM 425 optional. [1][2]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BCHM) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL)

question: how many credits is microbiology and what does the course cover
answer:
BIOL 311 Microbiology Lecture is 4 credits. [1] BIOL 311L Microbiology Laboratory is 1.5 credits; together, lecture and lab are 5.5 credits. [1][2]

The lecture covers the biology, chemistry, and genetics of microorganisms; their relations to other biological systems; their environmental roles; food, industrial, pharmaceutical, and applied microbiology; and general microbiological aspects of infectious diseases (host-parasite relations). [1]

The lab complements the lecture. It covers general and diagnostic microbiology techniques and epidemiology, including handling, culturing, and identifying microbes. Students also design, conduct, and report on an experiment answering a microbiological question. [2]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL311) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL311L)

question: should i major in chemistry or biology if i want to get into pharmacy school
answer:
If you’re aiming for Ramapo’s Pharmacy Early Acceptance Program with LECOM, Biology is the clearest fit: the program awards a Ramapo B.S. in Biology, and Ramapo lists a “Biology/Touro Pharm 3+4” track. [1][3] The pages don’t say that Biology is required for pharmacy school generally or that Chemistry is a bad choice; they don’t give a general recommendation between the two. [1][2][3]

For LECOM’s Pharmacy EAP, the pages say to apply separately from your Ramapo application (high school seniors may apply); complete LECOM’s online EAP application by April 1; and, if eligible, self-schedule an offered interview. A successful interview may lead to provisional acceptance. You need that provisional acceptance before starting your second undergraduate year. Phase II requires an overall GPA of 3.2 or higher and a science GPA of 3.0. To enter LECOM, submit a PharmCas application, complete three years of undergraduate study, and meet GPA and other requirements. The PCAT is encouraged, not required. The program is three years at Ramapo plus four years of pharmacy education. [3][6]

The Pharmacy EAP is handled by LECOM. Ramapo Admissions lists admissions@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7300. [3][6] For help choosing, the Center for Student Success recommends gathering information, talking with advisors and faculty, and meeting with your major’s convener when ready; contact success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441. [8] The Pre-Medical/Pre-Health Club welcomes aspiring pharmacists; email premed@ramapo.edu. [7]
